privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Readfox is a small, independently run service. This page says plainly what we store, who else touches your data, and what we can and cannot see.

items.account: Your email address, optional name, and a salted hash of your password.
items.text: The text extracted from books and articles you import (titles and chapters). We do not keep the original EPUB file.
items.learning: Your vocabulary, reading progress, practice history, journal entries and settings.
items.betaSignIn: If you sign in to Readfox Beta with your Readfox account, Beta receives your account identifier, verified email address and name. Beta keeps its own session and study data.
items.vocabTestReports: If you save a vocabulary test, we keep the estimated range, reference level, test date and suggested books in your account. Your answers stay in your browser.
items.readingStats: Your reading time and the number of words you read, stored in your learning statistics.
items.autoSave: The words you look up are saved to your word list automatically. You can turn this off in Settings.
items.timezone: Your browser's time zone. It is saved to your account to calculate your learning day, which sets your daily statistics and streaks. The same time zone sets when we send reminder emails.
items.reviewHistory: Your word review history: each answer, the time you gave it, and the card's schedule. It is part of your data export. Free accounts keep the most recent 5,000 entries.
items.usage: Monthly counters of how many AI lookups and requests you used, so we can apply the monthly allowance.
items.aiKey: If you add your own AI key, it is stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM). It is never sent back to your browser.
items.session: A session cookie that keeps you signed in, and server logs used to keep the service secure and working. Web access logs keep the page address, time and status, with the IP address cut to its first three parts (for example 203.0.113.x). They hold no cookies or passwords and are deleted after 30 days.
items.loginRecords: Sign-in records: the time, your browser's user-agent text and a shortened IP address. We keep only the first three parts of an IPv4 address (for example 203.0.113.0) and the first 48 bits of an IPv6 address.
items.sourceCounts: Anonymous daily counts of visits and sign-ups. Each count notes the kind of site that sent you (a named search engine, AI assistant or social site, from a fixed list) and your browser language group. A count has no link to an account, no IP address and no full referrer address. A first-party cookie named rf_src holds the channel and the language group for up to 30 days, so one browser counts once. When you sign up, the count for that channel goes up by one, still with no link to your account.
items.feedback: If you send feedback, we store the message text and email it to the operator with your account email address, so we can reply, and with any images you attach. The images are not stored. We delete the stored messages when you delete your account.
items.invites: Your invite code, who invited you or whom you invited (as an internal account link), and any reward cards you hold.
items.inviteFingerprint: If you earn an invite reward, we keep a keyed one-way hash of your email address for 24 months, even after you delete your account. It cannot be turned back into your address. It only stops the same address from earning the reward twice.
items.welcomeClaim: When you receive the welcome offer, we keep a one-way hash of your email address and a one-way hash of its domain. We keep them also after you delete your account. They cannot be turned back into your address. We use them to give the offer once per mailbox, and a few times per private domain.
items.sharedWords: A shared cache of single-word translations, dictionary meanings translated into a learner's language, translations of public example sentences (free-library books and Tatoeba), and AI-written example sentences for a word (the language pair, the word or public sentence, and its translation), reused for every account. It holds no account information and none of your sentences.
items.appData: This device keeps recently shown pages, such as your library, word lists and stats, and the five lessons you opened last. The iPhone app also keeps words you saved offline until they sync. Signing out removes all of this from the device. Deleting your account does the same when you next reach the sign-in page.
items.pushReminder: In the iPhone app, if you turn on the daily review reminder, we keep your phone's push token, your interface language and the reminder time. We use them only to send one notification a day that shows how many cards are due. Apple delivers it. Turning the reminder off removes the token. Deleting your account removes both.

others.heading: Who else is involved

items.cloudflare: Cloudflare – DNS, the Turnstile bot check on sign-up, and R2 storage for backups.
items.google: Google – if you choose Google sign-in, Google tells us your email address, your name and your profile picture, and that it has confirmed the email address. We use them to create your account or to sign you in. If an account with the same email address already exists, we merge the two, so you keep your data. If that account never verified its email address, we also remove its password and end its sessions. We also store your Google account ID and the sign-in tokens Google issues. We never receive your Google password.
items.resend: Resend – delivers the verification and password-reset emails. When product emails are on, it also delivers these emails: a welcome email; short reading reminders in the first days; a tip about word review and Anki after you save 10 words; a note when you reach the free monthly AI limit; and a reminder about words due for review. It also delivers a reminder 3 days before a plan with a fixed end date ends, such as a one-time RMB payment or a code. A plan that renews on its own gets no such reminder. Each of these emails has an unsubscribe link. It also delivers the PDF report to your verified account address when you ask to save a vocabulary test.
items.aiProvider: Your AI provider (OpenRouter or Anthropic) – if you add your own key and use translation, explanations or chat, the text you select, with some surrounding context, is sent to the provider using your key. Their privacy terms apply to that data, and the usage is billed to you.
items.aiBuiltIn: Alibaba Cloud (Model Studio) – if you use Readfox's built-in AI allowance instead of your own key, the text you select, with some surrounding context, is sent to Alibaba Cloud's Qwen models through our workspace to produce the translation or explanation. During word review, a public example sentence or the word being reviewed may also be sent, never a sentence you saved. Alibaba Cloud's terms apply to that data. The allowance is limited each month. To make lookups faster, Readfox may also send a few single words from the lesson you open, before you tap them. These are dictionary words only, never your own notes, journal or sentences. Your own key is never used for this. The server also keeps anonymous daily counts of AI lookup speed and cache hits, with no account and no text.
items.paddle: Paddle – our reseller (Merchant of Record) for card and PayPal payments. If you subscribe this way, Paddle collects your payment details and billing address under its own privacy policy. We receive your email address, your plan and its status, never your card or account numbers.
items.xiaodou: Xiaodou Pay (Yuzhi AI, Shenzhen) – processes one-time RMB payments through Alipay and WeChat Pay. It receives the order amount, an order number and the public IP address of your device. Your Alipay or WeChat account details stay with Alipay or WeChat; we never receive them.

others.noTrackers: We do not use advertising or third-party analytics trackers, and we do not sell your data.

operator.heading: What the operator can and cannot see
operator.dashboard: The admin dashboard shows account-level numbers (sign-up date, last activity, counts of lessons and words, storage used) and a masked email address such as xi***@gmail.com. It also shows service-wide daily totals, such as sign-ups, active learners, lookups, payments and visits by channel, which do not name any account. It does not show your name. It has no screen that displays your book text, and it has no “view as user” or per-user export feature. The operator can reveal a full email address to give you support, handle a deletion request or stop abuse. Each reveal is written to an audit log.
operator.access: Be aware that the operator still has technical access to the server and its database, so we cannot promise that viewing is technically impossible. We do not look at your content. If you ask for support and send us an export, we use it only to fix your problem and then delete it. Please do not upload material you would not want a server to process.

backups.heading: Backups
backups.body: The database is continuously replicated to Cloudflare R2, which encrypts data at rest. Daily snapshots are additionally encrypted with a key kept offline by the operator, and are kept for 30 days.

items.export: Export: Settings → Learning data → Export all learning data downloads everything you have stored.
items.delete: Delete: Settings → Delete account removes your account and data from the live service. One record stays: if you turned off product emails or used an unsubscribe link, we keep a one-way hash of your email address, so we never email that address again. It cannot be turned back into your address. One more record stays: if you received the welcome offer, we keep the one-way hashes of your email address and its domain, so the offer is given once per mailbox. Copies in backups disappear as the daily snapshots expire (up to 30 days).
items.aiKey: You can remove your AI key at any time in Settings.

children.heading: Children
children.body: Readfox is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their data.

contact.heading: Changes and contact
contact.body: If this policy changes in a meaningful way we will update the date above. Questions or requests about your data: <mail>privacy@readfox.app</mail>.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: By creating an account or using Readfox you agree to these terms. Readfox is a brand operated by a sole proprietor. In these terms, "Readfox", "we" and "us" mean that sole proprietor.

content.heading: Your content
content.body: You keep ownership of what you import. Only import text you have the right to use for personal study. You are responsible for the content you upload, and we may remove content or suspend accounts that infringe others' rights or abuse the service.

limits.heading: Limits
limits.body: What each account can use depends on its plan; the Pricing page lists the allowances. Free accounts can store up to 5 MB of imported lesson text, paid plans up to 100 MB. Audio and podcast import are not offered. AI features use either a key you provide, whose cost is yours, or the monthly allowance of your plan.

payments.heading: Paid plans, renewal and refunds
payments.body: You can pay in RMB with Alipay or WeChat Pay through Xiaodou Pay. When the Pricing page offers card checkout, you can also pay by card, PayPal or Apple Pay through Paddle. Paddle.com is our reseller and the Merchant of Record for those orders: it takes the payment, adds sales tax or VAT, sends the receipt and answers payment questions. Paddle's buyer terms also apply to those orders.
payments.renewal: Plans bought in RMB cover a fixed period and do not renew. Plans bought through Paddle renew each month or each year, as you chose, until you cancel. You can cancel at any time in Settings → Plan. The plan then stays active until the end of the period you paid for, and nothing more is charged. If the price of your plan changes, we tell you by email before the new price applies.
payments.refunds: You can ask for a refund of an RMB payment within 24 hours after you pay, once per account, if you used 10% or less of the plan's AI allowance since the payment. Press Request refund in Settings → Plan, or write to <mail>privacy@readfox.app</mail>. The full terms are on the <refund>Refund policy</refund> page. We may refuse a refund when we see signs of abuse.
payments.rmb: Buyers who pay in RMB with Alipay or WeChat Pay buy a fixed period (1 or 12 months) through Xiaodou Pay. These payments do not renew; when the period ends the account returns to Free. If you buy the same plan again before it ends, the new period starts when the current one ends.

acceptableUse.heading: Acceptable use
acceptableUse.body: Do not attack, overload or probe the service, create accounts in bulk, share your account, or use it to break the law.

warranty.heading: No warranty
warranty.body: The service is provided “as is”, without guarantees of availability or fitness for a purpose. Translations come from AI models and can be wrong. We make backups but you should export your data from time to time. To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for lost data or indirect losses.

termination.heading: Changes and termination
termination.body: We may change or end the service, and will try to give notice. You can delete your account at any time.

openSource.heading: Open source
openSource.body: The software is licensed under the GNU AGPL-3.0. See the About page for the source code.

about.title: About Readfox
about.intro: Readfox lets you read real books and articles in the language you are learning, translate words and phrases as you go, and turn what you meet into spaced-repetition practice.

freeSoftware.heading: Open source
freeSoftware.license: Readfox is open-source software under the <license>GNU Affero General Public License v3.0</license>. It is built on <lector>Lector</lector>, an open-source reader by heuwels and its contributors, with our changes.
freeSoftware.source: The complete source code of the version running on this site is available at <source>{url}</source>.

dataSources.heading: Data sources
dataSources.body: Sentence banks come from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR) and dictionaries from the sources listed in the repository README, each under its own licence.
dataSources.books: The free books in the library are public-domain texts from Project Gutenberg (gutenberg.org). The Korean books come from Korean Wikisource (ko.wikisource.org); their transcriptions are licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Each book links back to its source page.
dataSources.dictionaries: Dictionary meanings come from the English Wiktionary through kaikki.org (CC BY-SA). The English dictionary is built from ECDICT by skywind3000 (MIT licence, github.com/skywind3000/ECDICT), and its example sentences come from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
dataSources.readingFeed: Articles in the Free books dialog's News, Travel and Science tabs come from Global Voices (CC BY 3.0, globalvoices.org), Wikivoyage (CC BY-SA 3.0, wikivoyage.org), Simple English Wikipedia and Vikidia (CC BY-SA 4.0). Each article links to its licence and original source; adding one to your library appends that attribution.

refunds.title: Refund policy
refunds.intro: Readfox sells paid plans that give you a larger monthly AI allowance. This page says when you can get your money back.
refunds.rmbIntro: Each payment buys a fixed period of 1 or 12 months and does not renew.
refunds.rule1: You can ask for a refund within 24 hours after you pay.
refunds.rule2: Since the payment, you used 10% or less of your plan's monthly AI allowance. Word translations and detailed answers are counted on their own, and the higher share counts. Use before you paid does not count.
refunds.rule3: Each account can get one refund.
refunds.how: To ask, open Settings → Plan and press Request refund. The button shows only while you can still ask. If it does not work, write to <mail>privacy@readfox.app</mail>. We check each request, return the money to the account you paid with through Xiaodou Pay, and your plan returns to Free. The money can take a few working days to arrive.
refunds.after: After 24 hours, or when your use is above the limit, we do not refund the period. The plan does not renew, so nothing more is charged.
refunds.cardBody: Paddle.com is our reseller and handles these payments. You can get a full refund within 14 days after a payment, both for the first payment and for a renewal. Write to privacy@readfox.app with the email of your account, or use the support link in your Paddle receipt, or request a refund at paddle.net. A refund ends the plan at once and the money goes back to the card or account you paid with. After 14 days we do not refund the current period, but you can cancel at any time in Settings → Plan so the plan does not renew. Your legal rights as a consumer are not affected.
refunds.abuseBody: We may refuse a refund when we see signs of abuse, for example buying a plan, using the allowance, and asking for a refund again with new accounts.
